claim: Short-range wireless links reduce peripheral cabling.
originalWording: Short-range wireless links reduce peripheral cabling.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 12, printed p. 20

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Wireless links substantially displace short peripheral cables in ordinary use; “disappearing” describes a trend, not zero cables.
reference.rationale: Commercial Bluetooth keyboards/mice and ordinary Wi-Fi demonstrate the predicted transition by 2009. The broad direction holds. Charging leads and remaining monitor cables are not evidence that the trend failed.

evidence.title: Apple introduces wireless keyboard and mouse
evidence.note: Opening Bluetooth product description and cable-replacement feature paragraphs. Apple introduced Bluetooth keyboards and mice in September 2003, directly supporting peripheral cable substitution. Evidence limits: The release does not show that monitor cables or power leads were eliminated.

evidence.title: Wireless Internet Use — Pew Research Center
evidence.note: US adult survey. Ever-used wireless access is not a majority-of-traffic measure and is not global coverage.. US adult survey. Ever-used wireless access is not a majority-of-traffic measure and is not global coverage.

strict.criterion: The full listed peripheral set, including most displays, ordinarily communicates wirelessly.
strict.rationale: Wireless input and networking are established, but wired monitors and other peripherals preserve an important part of the listed ecology.
